turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hello, Doctor. Well, I came in today because I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. 

My kitchen table is completely covered right now with my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center, and all these half-finished lists. I sit down there to try and tackle it, and I just... I don't know which thing to do first. I end up just sitting there looking at it until the whole day is gone.

symptom_reasoning.S031: The patient describes severe indecisiveness, stating they do not know which task to do first and end up sitting there all day.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel that these problems started after your husband began needing more help?
turns.patient_response:
Well, they definitely got a lot worse when he needed more help, but... honestly, no, they didn't just start then. I've always struggled with this sort of thing, even way back when I was a little girl. 

I remember my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but... careless. I was always forgetting my books or my homework. They constantly had to remind me to just finish my seatwork before I was allowed to go outside. So, I guess it's always been there, it's just... it's just so much harder to manage now with everything else on my plate.
